properties.decision: On a durable open, refuse when the identity sidecar is absent AND the store directory already held data AND the legacy probe finds no design under the old shared id. "Already held data" is answered BEFORE the store is opened, from the filesystem alone: a `.sst` file, or a non-empty write-ahead log. Opening creates the directory, so the evidence exists for exactly one line. All three prior behaviours are unchanged — a sidecar that is present is read (and still refused if unreadable), a genuinely fresh store still mints, and a pre-identity graph under the shared id is still adopted.
properties.name: A lost identity sidecar is caught by what the filesystem can see, because the store cannot be asked what designs it holds
properties.rationale:
THE CHECK THIS REPLACES IS ONE WE CANNOT WRITE. The honest question is "does this store hold a design under ANY id", and it cannot be asked: graph_id namespaces every stored key and dynograph-storage exposes no enumeration of ids — count_nodes(graph_id, type) requires the very id you are trying to discover. dynograph-storage is pinned by git tag v0.12.0 in the workspace Cargo.toml, so acquiring that scan means a change to another repository, a new tag, and a bump here. That is a real option and it is the BETTER fix; it is not this fix.

"The store already held data, and it is not the legacy design" answers the same question from outside, with nothing but read_dir. It is a PROXY, and the ways it is wrong are worth stating rather than discovering: a store created and opened but never written, whose sidecar is then lost, is refused though nothing is at stake — the refusal names how to proceed, and the alternative (minting over a live design) is unbounded, so the tie breaks toward refusing. A store whose data files were deleted while the directory survived would not be caught, which is not a case a mis-scoped mount produces.

WHY A PROXY NOW BEATS THE REAL CHECK LATER. cap:hosted-state-on-a-volume is BUILT, not planned — art:dockerfile realizes it — and it already ships knowing this exact failure. Dockerfile:78-82 says so in capitals: a store opened without its identity sidecar "finds nothing and PRESENTS AS AN EMPTY DESIGN, reporting nothing wrong", and mounting `.../graph` rather than its parent "is a plausible-looking mistake that silently loses a project. MOUNT THE PARENT." The mitigation for a known silent-data-loss path was a comment addressed to the one person who cannot read it: the operator gets no error, because there is no error. The capability's own statement already says the required behaviour is to refuse.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, so nobody reads more into a green check: it does not RECOVER the design. The store still holds it, under an id nothing can now name. Recovery needs the sidecar restored from backup, or the scan above — at which point the id could be read back off the store and the refusal could become self-healing. That is the follow-on this defers, and the reason to prefer the foundation change eventually rather than instead.

The asymmetry it removes was already visible in the code: an UNREADABLE sidecar was refused with "reflow2 will not guess", while an ABSENT one minted silently — and absent is the likelier of the two on a mounted volume.
